_how_to_edit: Arm Lab (vibration test) data. Add a paddle to 'arm', 'offcenter' and/or 'stiffness', change 'updated', then run python3 build.py. Arm Score: higher = more arm-friendly, reference paddle = 100. Optional keys: photo (file in site/assets/paddles/product/), xray (slug in site/xray/), used, reference, second_tester (shows the 'Second tester' chip and the footnote in 'second_tester_note'), approx (stiffness value shown with ~).
arm_tested: Nov 21, 2026, one session (Franklin Dynasty Whip: Nov 23, second tester)
headline: The Evolv (6 months of use) and the RPM Jade are the most arm-friendly so far; both Grit E2 CF versions are the firmest.
second_tester_note: Tested Nov 23, 2026 by a second tester (Daniel), with the Grit E2 CF reference in the same session. Its numbers are scaled to the reference so they line up with this table: compare them loosely. It ties the Grit overall: less shock and twist (it's heavier, swingweight 122 vs 110), but more buzz from its softer face.
offcenter_lead: Off-center hits sent 38–114% more shock to the wrist than center hits; the Evolvs were the most forgiving and the RPM Jade the least.
offcenter_notes: The RPM Jade is the cleanest paddle on center hits (1.16 g) but jumps the most on mishits, which fits its low twistweight.
Off-center hits mainly add jolt and twist, not more buzz.
These were small mishits during center blocks, so bigger mishits may be worse.
Early results: 7–8 hits per group, so treat small differences as ties.
offcenter_second_tester: Franklin Dynasty Whip (second tester): off-center hits sent 40% more shock than center hits, the same as the Grit E2 CF in that session (+41%). It's shown as a note, not a row, because it was a different tester.
stiffness_title: RPM Jade has the stiffest face, Speedup Tide the softest

stiffness.flag: RPM Jade's buzz is dominated by a higher vibration mode; its value may overstate stiffness.

grip_test.title: Do grip upgrades protect your arm?
grip_test.lead: We tested Daniel's Franklin Dynasty Whip in six setups on Nov 23, 2026, with the Grit E2 CF reference at the start and end of the session so we could correct for player fatigue. Arm Score: Grit E2 CF = 100.
rows: Same shock; the paddle twisted about 24% more in the hand
No measurable benefit; adds about 17 g to the handle
+ 6 g lead (3 g at 3 and 9 o'clock)
About 14% less twist, a steadier paddle
grip_test.footnote: That run had softer ball contact, which inflates its score.
grip_test.limits: One player, one run per setup: treat these as trends, not proof.
grip_test.headline: No grip upgrade we tested reduced the shock or buzz reaching the wrist; a little lead tape made the paddle steadier.
details: No change in shock or buzz at the wrist. The thicker grip let the paddle roll slightly in the hand on off-center hits.
Compared with the same overgrip on a bare handle, no measurable change in shock (−4%) or buzz. It mainly adds weight to the handle.
Raised twistweight from 6.24 to 6.75 and made the paddle steadier, but didn't reduce shock.
Why grips can still feel better
Our sensors measure what reaches the wrist, not comfort in the palm. Grips are about feel, fit and sweat control, not shock protection.
For arm comfort, the paddle matters far more than the grip. The most arm-friendly paddles we've tested score 30–44 points higher; no grip change moved the score more than 5.

glossary_lead: Every number describes what one hit does to your arm, averaged over about 25 hits.
stiffness_notes: Weight also affects pitch (a lighter paddle rings higher), so this is face stiffness relative to the paddle's weight.
Franklin Dynasty Whip (second tester, Nov 23): about 350 Hz, a softer face than the new Grit E2 CF, in the same range as the older Grit (361 Hz) and the RPM V2 (345 Hz).
The Speedup Tide 14L has a 14 mm core.
